subject.title: Feature Request: Support YAML as config file format

question: Should OpenClaw support `openclaw.yaml`/`openclaw.yml` as first-class config files, or keep JSON5 `openclaw.json` canonical and invest in supported config editing tools/docs instead?
rationale: This expands the core on-disk config contract and changes compatibility, parser, write-back, and repair behavior; source inspection shows no broken existing behavior to repair automatically.

options.title: Keep JSON5 Canonical
options.body: Keep the single JSON5 config contract and improve docs/tooling around CLI config commands, Control UI editing, and `config.patch` for comment-preserving edits.

options.title: Design YAML Support
options.body: Accept YAML only after a maintainer-owned design covers file precedence, write-back format, includes, validation, security review, docs, and upgrade tests.

options.title: Defer Pending User Evidence
options.body: Leave the request low priority until real user workflows show existing config-editing paths are insufficient.

recommendation.title: Keep JSON5 Canonical
recommendation.body: Keep the single JSON5 config contract and improve docs/tooling around CLI config commands, Control UI editing, and `config.patch` for comment-preserving edits.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for config compatibility, migration, and recovery policy points to this owner area.
